Thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. We've sketched a starter rider that separates realtime API availability from batch/long-run job availability and includes a draft definition of degraded mode. High level proposals we want to validate with you:

- Realtime text/generation API SLO: 99.95% monthly availability (standard).
- Batch/long-running job SLO: 99.5% monthly availability (acknowledges scheduled job windows and longer scheduling queues).
- Degraded mode: defined as per-token latency > 2x baseline or throughput < 60% of committed capacity for > 5 consecutive minutes; triggers reduced credit schedule and fallback commitments.
- Credits: proportional to downtime bucket with a defined maximum per month; separate credit table for realtime vs batch workloads.
- Evidence: request for token-level traces, request/response IDs, KV cache hit/miss stats, and a signed runbook excerpt showing incident timeline.

I've attached our initial draft rider as "HelixOps_SLA_Rider_v1.docx" for your review (section comments active). Karthik / Soojin — can you review legal/ordering language and the evidence clauses? Jonas / Soojin —

Quick notes and suggested language we can present to HelixOps procurement (feel free to paste into the order form):

1) Measurement windows: "Realtime API availability" will be measured at the per-minute rolling window across the customer's primary region. "Batch job availability" will be measured per scheduled job window; for customers with scheduled batch windows >30 minutes we will compute availability over the window and aggregate daily. This avoids penalizing short spikes during long-running jobs.

2) Availability targets: Realtime API = 99.95% monthly. Batch jobs = 99.5% monthly when jobs are submitted through Redwood's batch API. We can offer a migration clause to move jobs to realtime SLA if the customer adopts streaming/interactive interfaces.

3) Degraded mode definition (recommended): Degraded mode is declared when any of the following are true for a continuous period of >5 minutes: (a) median per-token generation latency for the realtime API > 2x baseline for the rolling 5-minute period, (b) committed throughput for the Dedicated pool falls below 60% for >5 minutes, or (c) request queue length exceeds configured burst threshold and cannot be cleared within the configured burst time.

4) Credits: credits calculated as a percentage of monthly committed fees proportional to downtime buckets; separate caps for realtime (max 50% monthly credit) and batch (max 30% monthly credit). Credits are customers' sole remedy.

5) Evidence and retention: Acceptable evidence includes token-level traces with request IDs, cluster-level telemetry snapshots, and timestamps from the customer's runbook. Redwood will retain detailed telemetry for 90 days; summary telemetry for 365 days. For claims older than 90 days, customers must provide their own collected evidence.

6) Maintenance windows and notice: Redwood will provide a planned maintenance calendar for the Dedicated pool with at least 72 hours' notice for non-emergency maintenance and will use best-effort scheduling outside of known batch windows when requested. Emergency maintenance carveouts defined per MSA.

I'll attach a short evidence matrix for procurement to review. If HelixOps needs stronger batch availability we can propose a priced uplift.

Att: procurement-evidence-matrix.xlsx

Karthik Iyer
Head of Legal & Procurement Partnerships
